name: Abelina
classification_notes: Built on chancery and italic calligraphic models executed with a pointed brush, giving it the joined, gestural structure typical of a connecting script.
summary: A pointed-brush display script built around the spontaneity and speed of gestural handwriting.
description: Abelina reworks chancery and italic calligraphic models into a typeface, keeping the pattern-like rhythm of pointed-brush lettering. It began as a university typography project before Guillermo Vizzari redeveloped it into the fuller "Abelina Pro" with Sudtipos, adding over a thousand glyphs of alternates, ligatures and initials.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Abelina as a display face for titles that emulate gestural handwriting, originally a University of Buenos Aires typography thesis by Yanina Arabena later rebuilt as Abelina Pro.

name: Address Sans
classification_notes: Rooted in the condensed structure and block modulation of 1950s German street-signage lettering, giving it a mid-century grotesque character across a wide weight and width range.
summary: A mid-century grotesque built from 1950s German street-signage lettering, spanning seven weights in condensed, regular and extended widths.
description: Address Sans takes its bones from condensed German signage lettering of the early 1950s, then extends the idea across a full range of weights and widths in the manner of Butti and Novarese's work for 1960s Italian foundries. The result reads as confidently mid-century, at home in identity and editorial work that wants a period charm without looking dated.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Address Sans as evoking mid-century Modern design history, rooted in condensed 1950s German street-signage forms and reworked across a full family of weights and widths.

name: Adios Script
classification_notes: Draws on 1940s commercial lettering guides and is built almost entirely around swash variation, placing it with the ornamental end of connecting scripts rather than plain handwriting styles.
summary: An elaborate ornamental script drawn from 1940s commercial lettering guides, with a huge stock of swash alternates.
description: Adios Script takes its cue from mid-century commercial hand-lettering manuals and pushes the ornamentation further, with 43 variants of the lowercase h alone. Its 1,470 characters give near-limitless combinations of ascenders and descenders without the strokes colliding, and it earned a Type Directors Club Certificate of Excellence.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Adios Script one of Alejandro Paul's most technically refined faces, inspired by 1940s commercial lettering guides and expanded with a huge range of ornate swash forms.

name: Affair
classification_notes: A joined cursive script with swash-driven flourishing, sitting in the romantic/wedding end of connecting scripts.
summary: A flourished, connected cursive script built for wedding and invitation work.
description: Affair is a fluid, joined cursive with generous swash flourishing on ascenders and descenders. It suits stationery, invitations and packaging where a warm, handwritten sentiment is called for.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos presents Affair as an optimistic, flourish-heavy connected script for romantic and celebratory design work.

name: Aguafina Script Pro
classification_notes: A narrow, joined brush script with long ascenders and descenders, built for semi-formal display use rather than plain handwriting simulation.
summary: A semi-formal connecting script with a narrow lowercase and long extenders, pitched for packaging and editorial use.
description: Aguafina Script is graceful without tipping into casual, with characters that flow into one another for a saucy, confident rhythm. The narrow lowercase makes efficient use of space while long ascenders and descenders keep it legible, which the foundry positions well for product packaging, magazine work and book covers.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Aguafina Script as elegant but not overly casual, a narrow flowing script suited to packaging and glossy magazine work.

name: Aladin Pro
classification_notes: A calligraphic art deco display face with an eastern-inspired letter treatment, closer to lettering than a running script.
summary: A calligraphic art deco display face with an eastern touch, drawn for packaging and headline work.
description: Aladin combines art deco structure with an eastern calligraphic feel, its casual counters and friendly terminals giving it warmth rather than severity. The foundry suggests it for exotic food and drink packaging as well as posters and book jackets that want a sense of Eastern hospitality.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Aladin a calligraphic art deco face with an eastern touch, useful for packaging exotic coffees and teas as well as posters and book jackets.

name: Alma
classification_notes: A casual brush script with pointed, playful strokes and a slightly weathered feel, built with a large alternates set for OpenType-aware use.
summary: A wild-natured brush script that stays sharp and determined even at its most casual.
description: Alma's strokes are pointed but playful, giving it a slightly weathered, organic character rather than a polished calligraphic finish. It ships in OpenType format with a wide set of alternates for programs that support contextual substitution.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Alma as a wild-natured script from Koziupa's drawing and Paul's digitising, casual and pointed but still sharp.

name: Almond Script
classification_notes: A textured, weathered calligraphic script with tall extenders, closer to rough brush lettering than a formal copperplate hand.
summary: A rusty, textured calligraphic script with tall wind-bent extenders, built with packaging in mind.
description: Almond Script pairs a rough ancient-brush feel with slim, delicate capitals, giving it a scarred, wavy character that reads as both weathered and elegant. Koziupa drew it and Paul digitised it, and the foundry positions it squarely for product branding and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Almond Script calligraphy gone rusty and textured, a convergence of rough ancient brush strokes and modern Latin elegance built for packaging.

name: Almoneda
classification_notes: An elliptical, high-contrast display face drawn from found lettering on old Madrid market ephemera such as boxes, posters and books, closer to display serif than text serif.
summary: An elliptical, high-contrast display face inspired by uppercase lettering found on old Madrid market ephemera.
description: Almoneda takes its name from Madrid's El Rastro flea market, where designer Ales Santos found nineteenth and early twentieth-century boxes, posters and books carrying unusual uppercase letterforms and rare ligatures. Three weights and a variable version give it range for editorial and contemporary display work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Almoneda as a typographic find from Madrid's El Rastro flea market, translating old market ephemera lettering into a modern elliptical display face.

name: Amorinda
classification_notes: A connected script that swings between wild display energy and a smoother, more restrained hand depending on setting, with a full alternates set.
summary: A connected script that can scream wildly or blend in smoothly, built as a versatile display face.
description: Amorinda balances wild and disciplined in the same design, helped by a complete set of alternates that let it flex between loud and quiet settings. The foundry positions it for product branding through to signage work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Amorinda as a connected script that is wild and disciplined at once, versatile enough for branding and signage.

name: Angelus
classification_notes: A flowing script that reworks copperplate conventions into a more casual, fresh interplay of ascenders and descenders.
summary: A casual, modern take on copperplate script with a fresh interplay between ascenders and descenders.
description: Angelus loosens the formality of traditional copperplate scripts into something more relaxed while keeping its flowing structure. The foundry suggests it for package design, personalised stationery and book covers.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos positions Angelus as a more casual modern version of copperplate script, suited to packaging, personalised collateral and book covers.

name: Ansage
subcategory: grotesque with condensed and expanded widths
classification_notes: Draws on nineteenth-century Gothic type specimens rather than rationalist sans models, with closed strokes, a large x-height and short extenders typical of a grotesque built for compact settings.
summary: A compact, sturdy grotesque with 10 weights and three widths, built from a study of nineteenth-century Gothic specimens.
description: Ansage (German for "announcement") deliberately avoids a neutral rationalist feel, instead drawing closed strokes and regular forms from nineteenth-century Gothic type. A large x-height and short extenders keep it compact, with open terminals that gain expressiveness as weight increases across its Condensed, Regular and Expanded widths.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Ansage as a sans serif with a strong personality rather than a neutral rationalist face, built from ten weights and three widths for branding, posters and apps.

name: Antica
classification_notes: Sharp triangular serifs place it in the nineteenth-century Latin/wedge-serif tradition rather than a bracketed old-style or transitional serif.
summary: A sharp triangular-serif Latin face pushed across eight weights, from thin to black, with true italics.
description: Nineteenth-century Latin types traditionally came in a single weight, so Antica extends the wedge-serif form across a full range from thin to black, adding swashes, small caps and stylistic alternates the originals never had. The foundry aims it at stylised labels and formal editorial work alike.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Antica as an homage to nineteenth-century Latin wood type, expanded from a single weight into eight weights with true italics and added swash detail.

name: Antipoda
classification_notes: A grotesque built at extreme weights and widths, closer in spirit to late nineteenth-century sans origins than to a neutral contemporary grotesque.
summary: A grotesque display family pushed to extreme weights and widths, built for short reading at large sizes.
description: Antipoda takes its cue from the origins of late nineteenth-century sans serifs and pulls the letterforms toward opposite extremes: fat and thin, condensed and extended. Three weights, three widths and a variable font let it flex between quiet and maximum visual impact.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Antipoda a grotesque sans serif display family exploring opposites, intended for large sizes and short reading with strong visual impact.

name: Apothicaire
classification_notes: Modelled on a late nineteenth-century antique-style casting with a contemporary reworking, spanning condensed to expanded widths.
summary: A late nineteenth-century antique-style serif reworked across three widths and five weights, plus a variable file.
description: Apothicaire runs from condensed to expanded across five weights from light to extra bold, with an elegant small caps set, ball terminals and delicate swashes among its OpenType features. It covers a wide range of Latin-alphabet languages.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Apothicaire as inspired by a late nineteenth-century antique style, offered in three widths and five weights with a bonus variable format.

name: Aranjuez Pro
classification_notes: A high-contrast calligraphic display face mixing art deco structure with ornamental ligatures, closer to lettering than a running script.
summary: A calligraphic art deco display face mixing thick-and-thin contrast with ornamental swashes and alternates.
description: Aranjuez leans into art deco calligraphy with a heavy dose of thick-and-thin contrast, producing an upright, ornamental style with alternates, swashes and playful contrast treatments built in. The foundry suggests it for packaging and book covers where the message needs a controlled touch of class.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Aranjuez a neo-psychedelic cross of pseudo-wood deco and ornamental calligraphy, useful for packaging and book covers.

name: Argenta
classification_notes: A casual handwritten script with typographic refinements and a large alternates set, built for OpenType-aware use.
summary: A fresh, handwritten script with a playful character and a large set of alternate letterforms.
description: Argenta reads as casual and handwritten at first glance, but carries specific typographic detailing underneath. Its alternates are extensive enough to reward use in OpenType-aware layout applications.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Argenta handwritten and fresh, a playful script with an immensely useful array of alternate characters.

name: Atocha
classification_notes: A bouncy, informal brush script named for a Madrid street, built with a companion caps set rather than a weight ladder.
summary: A bouncy, informal brush script named after Madrid's Atocha street, with a matching caps set.
description: Atocha is designer Joluvian's third font and the first drawn since settling in Madrid, following earlier releases inspired by Venezuela and the Philippines. It reads as fun and expressive with a homemade, hand-drawn quality suited to packaging and casual branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Atocha as Joluvian's tribute to Madrid, drawn since establishing Patera Studio near the city's Atocha street and station.

name: Auberge Script
classification_notes: Modelled on historic French batarde and coulée penmanship rather than English copperplate, giving it a period calligraphic structure distinct from most Sudtipos scripts.
summary: A historic French batarde and coulée-style connecting script, built with several alternate basic letter sets.
description: Auberge Script draws on eighteenth and nineteenth-century French penmanship traditions such as batarde and ronde rather than the English copperplate hand more common among Sudtipos scripts. It comes with several alternate default glyph sets alongside a full Pro version, suited to invitations, menus and formal stationery.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Auberge Script within a lineage of historic French calligraphic hands, built for formal invitations, menus and stationery.

name: Avellana Pro
classification_notes: A bold, rounded brush-lettered display face aimed at packaging and logotypes rather than continuous script writing.
summary: A bold, creamy display face built for packaging and friendly logotypes, from headlines down to small text.
description: Avellana Pro is wild but smooth at once, designed to carry from bold headline sizes down to small print without losing its character. Its Pro version covers the majority of Latin languages.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos positions Avellana Pro as a bit wild but smooth and creamy, built for packaging and friendly logotypes.

name: Aventura
classification_notes: A heavy, rounded display script with stylistic alternates, built for food and packaging branding rather than running text.
summary: A round, seductive display script with a sugary character, built for food branding and packaging.
description: Aventura leans heavy and rounded, with plenty of stylistic alternates to heighten or soften its mood as needed. The foundry pitches it at food packaging, logotypes and headline work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Aventura burlesquely round and stylishly seductive, sugar-fixed and loving, with alternates to shift the tone.

name: Bakery Script
classification_notes: A casual brush script offered in both solid and outline forms, giving it two distinct display treatments of the same letterforms.
summary: A 1970s-flavoured brush script with sharp and rounded moments, sold in solid and outline versions.
description: Bakery Script started as an outline drawn by Angel Koziupa, refined and extended into a solid version by Alejandro Paul. Both carry ligatures and letter alternates, and the foundry suggests them for packaging design and outdoor or adventure-themed work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Bakery Script as a nod to the high spirits of the 1970s, sold in outline and solid forms for packaging and display use.

name: Balneario
classification_notes: Adapted from casual sign-painter lettering rather than formal calligraphy, with lowercase added to a historically caps-only sign-painting style.
summary: A friendly, casual brush script drawn from golden-age sign-painting lettering, with two weights and a caps set.
description: Balneario is a small tribute to a coastal tourist city, reworking the "casual letters" style used by sign painters and extending it with a full lowercase. Two weights plus a Caps version give it enough range for warm, informal branding work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Balneario a tribute to a coastal port city, adapting golden-age sign-painter casual lettering into a friendly, rhythmic script.

name: Barricada Pro
classification_notes: A loud, small-countered display face with curved serifs and swashes, sitting between slab and serif display conventions.
summary: A loud-voiced display face with small counters and curved, swashed serifs, now expanded to seven weights.
description: Barricada Pro has a solid, strong structure with small counters that give it real presence, softened by curved serifs and swashes. Fifteen years after its first release it has been expanded into seven static weights plus a variable file, aimed at branding and packaging work that needs to be both striking and legible.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Barricada Pro as loud-voiced with a solid structure, expanded from its original release into seven weights and a variable format.

name: Bayoneta Pro
classification_notes: A hand-cut, woodcut-like display alphabet rather than a script, built for expressive rather than legible-at-length settings.
summary: A hand-cut display alphabet with a knife-carved, Polynesian-inspired texture.
description: Bayoneta reads like carefully constructed lettering rather than a typeface in the conventional sense, its shapes suggesting hand-cut or woodcut origins. The foundry suggests it for book covers, skateboard graphics, protein bar packaging and theme park signage alike.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Bayoneta a handcut alphabet bridging knife-wielding kitsch and studied display lettering.

name: Bellas Artes
classification_notes: An inline art deco display face built from calligraphic curves, positioned for decorative rather than script-like use.
summary: An inline art deco display face built from calligraphic curves split into complementary halves.
description: Bellas Artes pairs Koziupa's recognisable brush curves with Paul's technical construction, each letter built from two halves that complete one another. The foundry positions it for packaging and book or music covers with a feminine, pre-war visual feel.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Bellas Artes as the meeting of Koziupa's curves and Paul's technical expertise with an art deco aesthetic.

name: Bellissima Script
classification_notes: A copperplate script modelled on a nineteenth-century Spanish calligraphy manual, distinguishing it from the brush-based scripts elsewhere in the catalogue.
summary: A refined copperplate script drawn from Ramón Stirling's 1844 Spanish calligraphy manual.
description: Bellissima Script began from a nineteenth-century lettering book, Bellezas de la Caligrafía, that also fed into Poem Script's capitals. Alejandro Paul pulled back from the original's exuberant ornamentation to work within a simplified copperplate structure, and the result won a Certificate of Excellence at the Communication Arts Typography competition.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Bellissima Script to Ramón Stirling's 1844 Spanish calligraphy manual Bellezas de la Caligrafía, simplified from its original exuberant ornamentation.

name: Bibliophile Script
subcategory: Round Hand and Italian capitals script
classification_notes: Combines Round Hand calligraphy with Italian capitals, an unusual pairing that sets it apart from Sudtipos's more common brush or copperplate scripts.
summary: A script marrying Round Hand calligraphy with Italian capitals, drawn from Louis Prang's nineteenth-century pages.
description: Bibliophile takes its raw material from pages by Louis Prang, the Prussian-American printer who also inspired the Prangs fonts, this time combining Round Hand lowercase with Italian capitals rather than the italic Didone pairing of that earlier project. Regular and Bold weights give it some range for stationery and editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Bibliophile as scrap-heap parts from Louis Prang's pages rebuilt into a typeface marrying Round Hand calligraphy with Italian capitals.

name: Biographer
classification_notes: An upright script that stays close to roman proportions rather than a slanted cursive, with swash flaring reserved for ascenders and descenders.
summary: A mild, upright script reminiscent of roman proportions, with swash flaring saved for its extenders.
description: Biographer keeps its calligraphy mostly toned down, staying closer to roman letter proportions than a full cursive slant, with occasional swashy flares on ascenders and descenders. It supports an extended range of Western and Eastern European, Baltic, Turkish, Maltese and Celtic languages, and the foundry suggests it for literary book covers and calm packaging.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Biographer as a mild upright script good for women's literature and poetry covers as well as calm packaging design.

name: Blog Script
classification_notes: A rough, hand-drawn brush script built to evoke DIY and blog-era handwriting rather than a polished calligraphic hand.
summary: A rough, DIY-flavoured brush script in two weights, built for casual, handmade branding.
description: Blog Script leans into the intentionally rough, handmade aesthetic that took over graphic design as digital culture pushed back with nostalgia for the physical and imperfect. Regular and Light weights give it a little range for posters, packaging and quote graphics.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos positions Blog Script within a DIY handmade aesthetic, a reaction to an increasingly minimalist digital future.

name: Bowling Script
classification_notes: Distils lettering by 1950s German lettering artist Bentele into a rounded, casual brush script, following on from the earlier Semilla project.
summary: A rounded, casual brush script following on from Semilla, with a bonus set of bowling-ball dingbats.
description: Bowling Script continues Alejandro Paul's interest in Bentele, an obscure 1950s German lettering artist previously distilled into Semilla, this time with a heavier, more casual brush treatment. A companion "Balls" set adds themed ornaments for sports and leisure branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Bowling Script as a follow-on from Semilla, again distilling the lettering of 1950s German artist Bentele.

name: Bravissima Script
classification_notes: A dynamic, wild brush script built for food packaging, in the same spirit as the foundry's other Koziupa/Paul 1970s-inspired scripts.
summary: A dynamic, wild 1970s-style brush script built for food packaging.
description: Bravissima channels traditional Koziupa calligraphy through Paul's technical execution, spiced up with OpenType alternates. The foundry pitches it specifically at food packaging, especially where the product is meant to feel hot and immediate.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Bravissima the dynamic and spirited embodiment of the 1970s, a personal favourite for food packaging design.

name: Brisa Pro
classification_notes: A fast, light handwritten script built to read as a scrawled note rather than a formal hand, covering a mood range from light to dark.
summary: A quick, scrawled handwritten script that swings between light nonchalance and darker urgency.
description: Brisa Pro reads fast and immediate, like a note left in a hurry rather than a considered calligraphic hand. Its character shifts with context, equally at home as a casual aside or something more pointed.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Brisa Pro as covering the space from light nonchalance to eerie darkness with unprecedented determination and speed.

name: Brownstone Sans
classification_notes: A monoline decorative sans that grew out of experiments with the Business Penmanship script, closer to a display letterpress sans than a neutral text grotesque.
summary: A decorative monoline sans that grew out of leftover shapes from the Business Penmanship script, with ornamental frames echoing Brooklyn ironwork.
description: Brownstone Sans emerged when Alejandro Paul found forms in his Business Penmanship script that didn't fit that typeface's Spencerian brief, later developed after research trips through Brooklyn and the New York Public Library's specimen collection. It comes in Thin, Light and the more ornamental Hole style, with matching decorative frames referencing Park Slope's ironwork.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Brownstone an original twenty-first-century design subtly infused with nineteenth-century decorative influences and Brooklyn architectural references.

name: Brownstone Slab
classification_notes: A slab-serif companion to Brownstone Sans with sturdy serifs added for a more solid, masculine feel, sharing its Victorian ironwork inspiration.
summary: A sturdy-serifed slab companion to Brownstone Sans, built from the same Victorian New York ironwork references.
description: Brownstone Slab takes the popular, award-winning Brownstone Sans and adds sturdy serifs for a slightly more solid, masculine presence. It ships in Light and Thin weights with matching ornamental frames, and over 1,500 glyphs including small capitals, swashes and ligatures across a broad set of Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Brownstone Slab as based on the popular Brownstone Sans, influenced by the Victorian ironwork and carved decoration of New York row houses.

name: Bubblegum Sans Pro
classification_notes: A loud, brush-lettered display face modelled on 1930s advertising lettering rather than a running script or sans skeleton.
summary: An upbeat, brushy display face channelling 1930s advertising lettering that sold everything to everyone.
description: Bubblegum Sans Pro bounces with the flavour-loaded energy of golden-age American advertising lettering. It covers all Latin-based languages and includes a set of alternates for extra variety.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Bubblegum Sans Pro a loud twenty-first-century shoutout to the kind of 1930s lettering that sold everything to everyone.

name: Buddies
classification_notes: A script built from an experiment between brush pen and pencil rather than a single calligraphic tool, giving it a varied x-height and an unpredictable, sketch-like structure.
summary: A brush-and-pencil script with a varied x-height and a daring, atypical uppercase set.
description: Buddies began as a piece of lettering rather than a planned typeface, mixing brush pen freshness with pencil quirks. Its lowercase dances across several x-heights while the uppercase carries surprising, atypical shapes that work well set in short all-caps lines, which the foundry suggests for packaging, fashion and editorial use.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Buddies as a humble, unpredictable invitation to the brush-letters universe, born from an experiment between brush pen and pencil.

name: Buffet Script
classification_notes: Digitised stroke by stroke from Alf Becker's 1941 sign-lettering alphabets rather than drawn fresh, giving it a connected, intertwined structure typical of hand-cut sign scripts.
summary: A connected sign-painter's script redrawn from Alf Becker's 1941 alphabets for Sign of the Times magazine.
description: Buffet Script digitises calligraphy by Alf Becker, widely regarded as one of the great American sign-lettering artists, whose 1941 alphabet had never before been converted to digital form. Every stroke and curve was redrawn by hand rather than scanned, given the intertwined swashes running through the original.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Buffet Script to fantastic calligraphy by Alf Becker, redrawn stroke by stroke since scanning was never an option for such intertwined lettering.

name: Burgues Script
classification_notes: Modelled on Louis Madarasz's late nineteenth-century American penmanship, placing it firmly in the Spencerian copperplate tradition rather than a brush-drawn style.
summary: A Spencerian copperplate script paying homage to Louis Madarasz, one of the most skilled American penmen of the nineteenth century.
description: Burgues Script is one of the foundry's bestsellers, built as a tribute to Louis Madarasz's legendary pen. It carries the delicate engraving quality and disciplined flourishing of formal American penmanship, suited to stationery, wedding and celebration work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Burgues Script as an ode to Louis Madarasz, whose penmanship has inspired schools of calligraphy for over a century.

name: Business Penmanship
classification_notes: Modelled on the Spencerian and Palmer Method business handwriting taught in nineteenth and early twentieth-century American commercial colleges, a monoline hand rather than a broad-nib calligraphic style.
summary: A two-weight script paying tribute to the Spencerian and Palmer Method business handwriting once taught in American commercial colleges.
description: Business Penmanship revives an era when handwriting was a core part of business education, referencing Platt Rogers Spencer's cursive method and the later Palmer Method that succeeded it. Regular and Bold weights give it a little range for stationery and signature-style branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Business Penmanship as an ode to the era when penmanship was a prized part of American business education.

name: Cafelatte
classification_notes: A deliberately unpolished, wood-type-like calligraphic display face rather than a smooth connecting script.
summary: An unpolished, wood-type-flavoured calligraphic display face with a darker, unconventional edge.
description: Cafelatte offers a somewhat rough calligraphic concept reminiscent of wood type, built from Angel Koziupa's brush and refined through Alejandro Paul's curve work. The foundry positions it for packaging designers after a darker, more unconventional touch.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Cafelatte as offering a discerning packaging designer a refreshing, darker, unconventional touch.

name: Calgary Script
classification_notes: Inspired directly by a hand-painted welcome sign and years of American sign-painting reference books, giving it a caps-led sign-lettering structure rather than formal calligraphy.
summary: A speedy, sign-painter's brush script inspired by a hand-painted Welcome to Calgary sign.
description: Calgary Script pairs heady capitals with a free-flowing lowercase for a determined, fast-moving feel, drawing on years of American sign-painting reference. Ligatures, alternates and number-following ordinals give it a genuine supermarket-sign spin for packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Calgary Script to a brush-lettered Welcome to Calgary sign, filtered through decades of American sign-painting books.

name: Calicanto
classification_notes: A compact serif with a vertical stress axis, symmetrical curves and low contrast, designed specifically for newspaper and book text rather than display use.
summary: A compact, low-contrast serif built for newspaper and book text, with open counters and a generous x-height.
description: Calicanto is Alejandro Freitez's first commercial typeface, built on strong serifs, a vertical stress axis and slightly condensed proportions that suit dense-setting news and editorial work. Twelve variables each carry 750 glyphs across more than 90 languages, with small caps, ligatures and both lining and old-style figures for demanding text composition.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Calicanto as inspired by contemporary serifs and newspaper typography, ideal for combining across digital and printed media.

name: Candombe Pro
classification_notes: A brush-lettered display face named for an Afro-Uruguayan drum rhythm, with dancing, wild forms closer to lettering than a running script.
summary: A festive, brush-lettered display face named after the Afro-Uruguayan candombe rhythm.
description: Candombe conveys an upbeat, youthful spirit through unique dancing forms with wild brush-lettered origins. Its spontaneity suits signage, titles and greeting cards.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos names Candombe for the Afro-Uruguayan drum-based rhythm, conveying both an upbeat spirit and youthful joy.

name: Candy Script
classification_notes: Drawn from the tradition of hand-painted shop-window signage, with thick brush strokes rather than a fine calligraphic line.
summary: A thick, hand-brushed script capturing Argentina's window sign-painting tradition.
description: Candy Script draws on the country's shop-window sign-painting culture, its thick brushed characters carrying alternates for almost every letter. Over 1,150 characters and a full set of OpenType alternates give it plenty of variation for display and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Candy Script as inspired by Argentina and its culture, coming from window sign-painting tradition with a personality all its own.

name: Cascabel
classification_notes: A modular, building-block display alphabet built for architectural, maze-like word shapes rather than a conventional letterform structure.
summary: A modular, block-built display alphabet that reads as architectural when set in full words.
description: Cascabel is built on modular harmony, its maze-like geometric structures suggesting a building-block concept rather than conventional letterforms. It suits magazines, posters and flyers looking for a strong graphic structure.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Cascabel a maze-like geometric alphabet with an unmistakable architectural approach when set as complete words.

name: Cenizas
classification_notes: A wild, rough-and-tumble script recalling mid-twentieth-century English display scripts, filtered through a Latin brush sensibility.
summary: A rough-and-tumble script recalling mid-twentieth-century English display scripts, filtered through Latin brush humour.
description: Cenizas is casual, care-free and adventurous, suited to design around active pursuits like outdoor sports and travel. Its roughness also lends itself to art book and historical novel covers, museum literature and map design.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Cenizas as another masterpiece of rough-and-tumble script from the Koziupa and Paul partnership.

name: Chicle Pro
classification_notes: A bold, bouncy bubble-letter display face aimed squarely at kids' and confectionery packaging rather than editorial or corporate use.
summary: A bold, stretchable bubble-letter display face, Spanish for bubble gum and built to survive candy and toy packaging.
description: Chicle is a playful break from the foundry's more polished packaging fonts, built bold and kid-proof enough to handle the busy artwork of candy, cereal and toy boxes. The name is Spanish for bubble gum, and the design lives up to it.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Chicle bold, stretchable, kid-proof, pet-resistant letters, a definite sugar fix with no substitutes.

name: Chimango
classification_notes: A high-contrast serif built for headline and identity use, reinterpreting classic stroke-contrast principles rather than following one historical model.
summary: A high-contrast serif built for headlines and identity work, spanning six weights from Light to Extra Bold.
description: Chimango balances tension and fluidity between expressive forms and a clear underlying structure, built from classic stroke-contrast principles rather than a specific historical revival. Lighter weights bring flexibility while the heavier end amplifies its visual impact, giving it presence across editorial and identity applications.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Chimango as a typeface with presence, built to take centre stage in headlines, visual identities and editorial work.

name: Chocolate Pro
classification_notes: A brush-lettered display face offering three alternate letterform flavours within a single OpenType file rather than a weight ladder.
summary: A confectionery-branding display face offering three alternate letterform flavours in one OpenType file.
description: Chocolate Pro bundles three distinct letterform sets, from the bittersweet Amargo to the sweeter Dulce, accessible through OpenType alternates in a single font. It is built for food and confectionery packaging and branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos offers Chocolate Pro in three irresistible flavours, from bittersweet Amargo to mouth-watering Dulce, all in one OpenType file.

name: Ciabatta
classification_notes: Built on classical italic structure with double-storey alternates, positioned as a packaging display face rather than a text italic.
summary: A creamy, narrow display face for food packaging, based on classical italic shapes across five weights.
description: Ciabatta's slightly narrow forms are based on classical italic structure but offer two-storey a and g alternates for a more formal upright appearance. Five weights make it powerful enough for headlines while staying legible in small packaging text.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Ciabatta a creamy type especially made for packaging, powerful in headlines yet legible in small text.

name: Clockmaker
classification_notes: References turn-of-the-twentieth-century Victorian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco advertising type, particularly John F. Cummings' unreleased Elandkay design, across a full multi-weight family.
summary: An eight-weight vintage display face drawing on Victorian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco advertising type.
description: Clockmaker takes special influence from John F. Cummings' all-caps Elandkay, a design never digitised before, developing its uppercase first before extending down into a full range of weights. Its charming uppercase ligatures and support for Latin languages make it well suited to vintage-flavoured branding and book design.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Clockmaker as an eight-weight family inspired by Victorian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco advertising type, with a diverse and playful set of uppercase ligatures.

name: Coche
classification_notes: A connected script built with a corporate rather than romantic brief, meant for logotype use with a full small caps set.
summary: A connected script with a corporate feel, built to fill a gap in modern product branding and logotype work.
description: Coche means "automobile" in Spanish, and the design suggests exactly that kind of logo application. It comes loaded with alternates and a complete small caps set that complements the caps and lowercase for mix-and-play typography.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Coche as a connected script with a strong corporate feeling, aiming to fill a gap in modern product branding.

name: Compendium
classification_notes: A companion piece to Burgues Script that looks to Platt Rogers Spencer's earlier ornamental penmanship rather than Madarasz's later refinement.
summary: An ornamental Spencerian script tracing the penmanship style that gave rise to Burgues Script's later Madarasz influence.
description: Compendium sits as both sequel and prequel to Burgues Script, looking to Platt Rogers Spencer's Ohio-originated flourished hand that predates and underlies Madarasz's later refinements. It suits certificates, diplomas and romantic stationery work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Compendium as tracing Spencerian penmanship back to its roots, the groundwork for the calligraphic method Madarasz later developed.

name: Condiment
classification_notes: A soft, powdered-shape brush-drawn display face built specifically for food packaging branding.
summary: A soft, powdery brush-drawn display face built to add flavour to food branding.
description: Condiment mixes soft shapes with brush-drawn letters and a set of tasty OpenType alternates. It supports a broad Latin-based language range including Central European, Baltic, Turkish and Welsh.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Condiment as prepared from powdered soft shapes mixed with brush-drawn letters and tasty alternates.

name: Confitería
classification_notes: An upright, connected script named for traditional Buenos Aires confectionery shops, closer to delicate piped lettering than a brush or copperplate hand.
summary: An upright, connected script that brings to mind lettering piped onto delicate cakes, named for Buenos Aires confectionery shops.
description: Confitería is Spanish for a shop selling sweets and chocolates, often with a tea room attached, and the typeface captures that simple, unhurried charm. It suits restaurant branding, menus and stationery looking for a cute, feminine tone.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos quotes designer Julieta Ulanovsky describing Confitería as bringing to mind lettering piped on delicate cakes, sweet but never sickly.

name: Cooked
classification_notes: A rough, gory-feeling display alphabet built for Halloween and horror-themed use rather than food branding despite its culinary name.
summary: A juicy, rough-edged display alphabet built for horror and Halloween-flavoured design work.
description: Cooked is meant to induce a visceral reaction, suited to packaging, posters, books or music covers that stress the wild and adventurous side of life. A generous set of alternates for each letter keeps its rough character varied.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Cooked a stir-fried and juicy alphabet designed to crank up the senses of smell and taste.

name: Cosmos Deco
classification_notes: Modelled on architect Carlos Crombé's sketches for Mexico City's Cine Cosmos facade, an Art Deco sans with wide apertures for readability at text sizes.
summary: A nine-weight Art Deco sans modelled on architectural sketches for Mexico City's Cine Cosmos.
description: Cosmos Deco captures the clean lines and bold curves of Mexico City's early twentieth-century golden age of cinema architecture, with an uppercase built for heading impact and a lowercase with wide apertures for comfortable reading. Over 800 glyphs, stylistic alternates, small caps and both tabular and old-style figures suit editorial, museum and packaging use.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Cosmos Deco to Carlos Crombé's sketches for the original facade of the iconic Cine Cosmos, a symbol of Mexico's golden age of cinema.

name: Courtesy Script Pro
classification_notes: Modelled on the understated Zanerian school of Spencerian penmanship, with a monoline lowercase distinct from the more flourished capitals.
summary: A Zanerian-school Spencerian script with an understated monoline lowercase and flourished capitals.
description: Courtesy Script is based on an alphabet found in a nineteenth-century penmanship journal, its wide monoline lowercase connections keeping it readable while the capitals range from merely fancy to full engrossing flourish. It won a Certificate of Excellence at the Communication Arts Typography competition.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Courtesy Script as capturing the elegance and propriety of finely practiced Spencerian penmanship, particularly the Zanerian school.

name: Cuisine
classification_notes: Drawn from a 1950s how-to lettering book depicting early twentieth-century food and beverage label scripts, aimed at luxury food packaging.
summary: A creamy, hand-scribed script drawn from a 1950s lettering guide, suited to luxury food packaging and menus.
description: Cuisine suggests the label lettering found on early twentieth-century food and drink packaging, doing for food advertising what Bodoni does for fashion. Its hand-scribed charm suits high-end menus and luxe packaging alike.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Cuisine's simmering, hand-scribed charm captures the complexity of wine and the full-bodied energy of coffee.

name: Cupcake
classification_notes: A bold, creamy brush display face pitched at food and service branding rather than a running script.
summary: A creamy, bold display face for those with a sweet tooth, built for food and service branding.
description: Cupcake flares the taste buds with a construction designed to make sandwiches, pasta and desserts alike look appealing on packaging. It covers all Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Cupcake a font for those with a sweet tooth, designed to appeal to the masses of the food and service industries.

name: Darka
classification_notes: Blends the balance of Textura, the flow of Fraktur and the lowercase-to-uppercase ratio of Bâtarde into an original calligraphic blackletter.
summary: A gothic, calligraphic blackletter blending Textura, Fraktur and Bâtarde into an original design with a Mexican soul.
description: Darka began as personal calligraphic hand-lettering before evolving into a digital typeface with alternate glyphs and flourishes that preserve its hand-written tension. Sharp terminals and seductive curves make it work at both display sizes and, more unusually for a blackletter, in short text settings.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Darka a splendid, mysterious original blackletter, winner of an Award of Excellence at the Type Directors Club of New York.

name: Decoupe
classification_notes: A gestural sans inspired by paper cut-outs and spontaneous handwriting, with asymmetrical contrasts that emerge at large display sizes.
summary: A gestural display sans inspired by paper cut-outs, revealing asymmetrical contrasts at large sizes.
description: Découpe is built specifically for big display sizes, its irreverent, effervescent character breaking into visible contrasts and asymmetry as it scales up. Four weights with matching italics run from Light to Extra Bold, and the design has been shown in exhibitions including Tipos Latinos and the Type Directors Club.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Découpe as inspired by gestural graphic expressions like paper cut-outs, built to shout it out loud and clear.

name: Delight Script
classification_notes: An upright script drawn from post-WWII advertising conventions, casual and bouncy rather than a formal connecting hand.
summary: A casual, bouncy upright script drawing on post-WWII advertising scripts.
description: Delight Script is fresh and playful, built with plenty of alternates so every word can look like genuine hand lettering. It covers all Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Delight Script as a fresh and original design taking its cue from post-WWII advertising scripts.

name: Dilemma Sans
classification_notes: Inspired by anonymous early-1900s Peignot Foundry designs (Polyphème, Cyclopéen, Extra Condensé), built as a grotesque half of a paired sans/serif system rather than a standalone family.
summary: The sans half of the Dilemma system, a 21-style workhorse grotesque across three widths and seven weights, built to pair with Dilemma Serif.
description: Dilemma Sans reimagines anonymous early-1900s Peignot Foundry designs as a contemporary grotesque, sold as the sans counterpart to Dilemma Serif with which it shares proportions and spacing. Seven weights across Condensed, Regular and Expanded widths cover everything from economical condensed text to opulent expanded display, and the complete Dilemma family adds a variable format.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Dilemma a workhorse system where each style functions well alone but becomes more powerful pairing the sans with the serif.

name: Dilemma Serif
classification_notes: A serif built on the same skeleton as Dilemma Sans rather than a historical serif model, sharing its early-1900s Peignot Foundry references.
summary: The serif half of the Dilemma system, sharing its structure with Dilemma Sans across three widths and seven weights.
description: Dilemma Serif takes the sans skeleton of its sibling and adds serifs, rather than starting from a separate historical serif model, so the two pair cleanly in the same layout. It spans the same Condensed-to-Expanded width range and Thin-to-Black weight range as Dilemma Sans, aimed at identity systems, editorial and public-space work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Dilemma Serif as the other half of a workhorse system designed to pair sans and serif styles for maximum flexibility.

name: Diplomatic
classification_notes: A calligraphic connecting script relying on simplicity rather than heavy ornamentation, with prominent extenders driving its elegance.
summary: A calligraphically simple connecting script reaching for elegance through prominent extenders rather than heavy ornament.
description: Diplomatic pairs calculated but casual strokes with prominent ascenders and descenders for an unmistakably elegant setting. It suits menus, music packaging and romantic stationery.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Diplomatic another script from the Koziupa and Paul duo, relying on calligraphic simplicity to reach its artistic sophistication.

name: Distillery
classification_notes: A five-font collection (Display, Strong, Script, Caps and Icons) drawing on Arts and Crafts, Roman majuscules, tattoo lettering and 1970s handmade-label trends rather than one single letterform model.
summary: A five-font DIY hand-lettered collection spanning Display, Strong, Script and Caps styles plus icons and ornaments.
description: Distillery draws on Arts and Crafts lettering, Roman majuscules, traditional tattoo work, sign painting and early-1900s showcards, filtered through 1970s American handmade-label trends. The four text fonts work individually or together, backed by a wide range of alternates, ligatures and ornamental icons.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes the Distillery Set as strongly hinting at the spontaneous ways of pencil on paper, the dynamic rebellion and imperfection of DIY.

name: Divina
classification_notes: A Latinised digitisation of Rudolf Koch's 1927 Kurrent, a German school-writing blackletter script rather than a Textura or Fraktur style.
summary: A Latinised revival of Rudolf Koch's 1927 Kurrent, the German school-writing hand, digitised here for the first time.
description: Divina takes Koch's Kurrent, cut in 1935 as a model for German school handwriting, and adapts its all-connecting blackletter calligraphy for Latin typesetting. It marks the first digitisation of this particular Koch design.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Divina a Latinized digitization of German calligraphy master Rudolph Koch's Kurrent, never before digitised.

name: Dobro
classification_notes: A six-font display set including a colour font, drawing on bluegrass gig-poster wood type rather than a single letterform tradition.
summary: A six-font wood-type display set inspired by bluegrass music and vintage gig-poster lettering, including a colour-font version.
description: Dobro is meant for large sizes, coming in four weights plus a colour font (Drunk) with connectors and miscellaneous ornaments, alongside frames and borders that pay tribute to vintage wood-type catalogues. The set is built around rhythm and repetition, translating the feel of bluegrass music into a typographic system.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Dobro as inspired by the spirit of bluegrass music and the aesthetic of its wood-type gig posters.

name: Downtempo
classification_notes: A squarish, industrial-feeling sans with a distinctive ch ligature and Spanish-specific characters, built across three weights with a notable italic.
summary: A squarish, industrial-feeling sans in three weights, with a distinctive ch ligature and a notable italic.
description: Downtempo carries a deliberately industrial character across its three weights, with unique characters including a ch ligature and other Spanish-language-specific glyphs. Its italic style stands out as a particular design feature.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Downtempo as a 3-weight industrial-feeling font family with unique characters and a really special italic style.

name: Dr Carbfred Pro
classification_notes: Part of the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, built by assembling different signatures into full alphabets, a documentary calligraphic approach rather than a single designer's hand.
summary: A revived Bluemlein Script Collection design, assembled from historic American hand-lettering signatures and given a fictitious name.
description: Dr Carbfred Pro belongs to the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, originally built in the early twentieth century by collecting individual signatures and constructing complete alphabets from them, then presented under invented names in Higgins Ink catalogues. Sudtipos expanded the collection into digital versions for modern invitation and stationery use.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos revives the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, an intriguing reminder of the heady days of hand lettering in the United States before photo lettering took over.

name: Dr Sugiyama Pro
classification_notes: Another entry in the Bluemlein Script Collection, built the same way from collaged historic signatures rather than a single calligraphic hand.
summary: A second Bluemlein Script Collection revival, built from historic signature fragments assembled into a full alphabet.
description: Dr Sugiyama Pro shares its origin with Dr Carbfred Pro in the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, assembled from professional New York hand letterers' signatures before that trade was replaced by photo and digital lettering. Sudtipos expanded it into a modern digital format for invitations and stationery.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos brings the Bluemlein scripts back to life in a set of expanded digital versions drawn from historic Higgins Ink catalogues.

name: Dystopian
classification_notes: A black-and-white geometric sans that mirrors the colour font Utopian, both built on Bauhaus, De Stijl and Art Deco geometric principles.
summary: A black-and-white geometric sans built on Bauhaus and De Stijl principles, the darker sibling to the colour font Utopian.
description: Dystopian shares its structure with Utopian but carries an opposite, darker mood, the pair together reflecting divided visions of the future. It comes in Light, Regular, Bold and Black weights, with the two typefaces sold as a bundle that includes a colour-font version.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Dystopian as Utopian's close sibling in structure but with a darker look and feel, both inspired by Bauhaus, De Stijl and Art Deco.

name: Eclectica
classification_notes: Deliberately resists Humanist, Rational or Transitional classification, mixing abrupt angular modulation with classical proportions and an unusually disruptive tilting italic.
summary: A serif that refuses easy classification, mixing angular modulation and asymmetrical serifs with an unusually disruptive italic.
description: Eclectica mashes up writing and type theory rather than following one historical model, its abrupt modulation and unexpected serif asymmetries sitting against otherwise classical proportions. The italic breaks its uppercase down strokes to form a running bridge through the stems, giving noticeably more dynamism than the roman.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Eclectica doesn't worry about labels, refusing to be boxed into type classification while still nodding to tradition.

name: Elisetta
classification_notes: Draws structural cues from musical notation and neoclassical text serifs, built for extended reading in books and musical scores alike.
summary: A neoclassical text serif that blends the rhythm of musical notation with high-readability book typography.
description: Elisetta emerges from the shared vocabulary of musical notes and letterforms, taking on the neoclassical characteristics of current musical notation rather than any particular musical genre. Six variables, a Display cut with small caps, and true italics give it range for long-form text and sheet music alike.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Elisetta as designed specifically for the writing of texts and musical sheets, with high line performance and great readability.

name: Elvira Serif
classification_notes: A traditional serif skeleton fitted with sharp points and ink traps, built across nine weights for both display and small book-text sizes.
summary: A nine-weight display serif with sharp points and ink traps, built to feel sturdy in black and elegant in light.
description: Elvira Serif keeps the formality of a traditional serif but adds ink traps and sharp glyph details for a slightly more playful edge. True italics and a variable version give it enough range to run from web and headline use down to small book-publishing sizes.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos, working with Vástago, built Elvira Serif to make display serifs a little more fun while keeping the formality of a traditional serif.

name: Enterline
classification_notes: Based directly on illustrator Sael's own artistic signature, sold as both a colour font and a black-and-white OTF.
summary: A colour-font typeface built from illustrator Sael's own artistic signature lettering.
description: Enterline is based on the lettering of artist Sael, produced in collaboration with Alejandro Paul. It ships as both a colour SVG font for supporting design applications and a standard black-and-white OTF for general use.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Enterline as a collaborative typeface based on the lettering of Sael, available as both a colour font and black and white OTF.

name: Envelove
designer: Yanina Arabena, Guillermo Vizzari, Alejandro Paul
classification_notes: A free, spontaneous pointed-nib script following no formal calligraphic model, sold as three related fonts (Script, Caps, Icons) rather than a weight ladder.
summary: A free, spontaneous pointed-nib script that began as a personal calligraphy game, sold as a three-font set with caps and icons.
description: Envelove grew from Yanina Arabena's carefree pointed-nib, black-ink calligraphy, developed with Guillermo Vizzari and Alejandro Paul into a typeface that follows no formal calligraphic model. It combines three fonts, Envelove Script, Caps and Icons, aimed at romantic and celebratory stationery work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Envelove a play on words that reflects the love of letters, an expressive free-and-easy typeface that lets itself go with rhythm and sensation.

name: Epica Sans
subcategory: humanist sans companion to a Venetian serif
classification_notes: A contemporary humanist sans built as the counterpart to Epica Serif's Venetian Renaissance structure, retaining calligraphic reminiscences within a sans skeleton.
summary: A contemporary humanist sans completed in 2020 as the counterpart to Epica Serif's Venetian Renaissance structure.
description: Epica Sans carries calligraphic reminiscences into a sans skeleton, legible at both small text and display sizes. Designed to enrich the earlier Epica Serif rather than stand entirely apart from it, it gives the combined family more options for hierarchy and composition across books, editorial and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Epica Sans as completed in 2020, the sans counterpart designed to enrich and complement Epica Serif.

name: Epica Serif
classification_notes: A contemporary interpretation of Venetian Renaissance serif types, sketched during a Master of Type Design at the University of Buenos Aires and refined over several years.
summary: A contemporary Venetian Renaissance serif with calligraphic reminiscences, legible from small text to display sizes.
description: Epica Serif first took shape as sketches made during a Master of Type Design at the University of Buenos Aires, then went through several redesigns before reaching its current form. It combines the elegance of antique typography with contemporary functional balance, well suited to books, editorial work and branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Epica as a contemporary interpretation of Venetian Renaissance types, with the Serif finished in its first version five years before the Sans counterpart.

name: Esmeralda Pro
classification_notes: Rooted in Roman capitalis monumentalis stone-carved capitals combined with foundational brush-written lowercase, giving it a titling-serif character rather than a script structure.
summary: A titling display face rooted in carved Roman capitalis monumentalis, paired with a foundational-calligraphy lowercase.
description: Esmeralda combines the carved stone letterforms of Roman capitalis monumentalis with a brush-written foundational-calligraphy lowercase, redefining both under a shared structure. More than eleven hundred glyphs and a large ligature set mix classic proportions with a more contemporary impression.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Esmeralda to the classical capitalis monumentalis carved in stone, combined with a lower case built on foundational calligraphy.

name: Espiritu
classification_notes: An entirely hand-drawn illustrated lettering family with Condensed, Regular, Expanded, Script and Dingbats styles rather than a conventional weight ramp.
summary: A hand-illustrated lettering family evoking wanderlust and road trips, in Condensed, Regular, Expanded and Script styles plus dingbats.
description: Espíritu is entirely made by hand, its five styles guided by the impulse of the hand rather than a rigid drafting process, down to its accompanying icon set. It carries a free, imperfect and unpretentious spirit suited to motorcycle, drinks and lifestyle branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Espíritu as guided by the impulse of the hand, its soul deeply rooted in wanderlust and the enjoyment of the journey.

name: Evergreen
classification_notes: A pair of illustrative nature-themed inline display fonts (Dawn and Dusk) plus an icon set, closer to decorative illustration than conventional lettering.
summary: A nature-illustrated inline display pairing, Dawn and Dusk, with a matching icon set of leaves and flowers.
description: Evergreen praises nature around the clock with two complementary fonts, one for daylight and one for night, both wrapped in leafy, botanical detail. Butterflies and flowers join the icon set for organic, nature-branded packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Evergreen local, organic and certified free trade, twenty-four-seven-three-sixty-five of wild leafy character.

name: Fan Script
classification_notes: A bold, swash-driven script styled after mid-century sports team branding and baseball ephemera.
summary: A bold, swash-heavy script styled after vintage sports team branding, inspired by Argentina's football obsession.
description: Fan Script channels the retro, hand-painted lettering found on old sports club and team ephemera, strong enough to carry logotypes and headlines. Alternates and swashes keep it feeling authentically hand-lettered.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Fan Script within a nation obsessed with sport, particularly fútbol, built for club and team branding.

name: Feel Script
classification_notes: Digitises calligrapher Rand Holub's lettering for his Intertype face Monterey, redrawn from vintage American magazine ads, now expanded to three weights.
summary: A revival of Rand Holub's Monterey lettering for Intertype, now in three weights with three-letter ligatures and dreamy swashes.
description: Feel Script presents Holub's original lettering in full, some letterforms redrawn from vintage American magazine advertisements he lettered himself, alongside many new alternates and ending forms. Building on experience from Ministry Script, Affair and Burgues Script, Alejandro Paul extended the treatment with three-letter ligatures and extensive swash options.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Feel Script to lettering that calligrapher Rand Holub created for Intertype's Monterey face, now updated to three weights.

name: Felipe
classification_notes: A soft brush script made in memory of the designer's brother, with unusual majuscule and figure forms lifted from minuscule conventions.
summary: A soft, bittersweet brush script with playful, unconventional capitals, made in memory of the designer's brother.
description: Felipe contains fresh perspectives on old characters, with some majuscules and figures showing traits normally reserved for lowercase letters. Its bittersweet overall colour suits packaging, signage and culinary design.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos notes Felipe was made in the memory of Angel Koziupa's brother, softening his brush once again for a packaging-friendly, versatile font.

name: Festival Script Pro
classification_notes: Extends the deco-script territory of Aranjuez and Bellas Artes with a more geometric sensibility and ribbon-like strokes referencing Argentine filete motifs.
summary: A deco-inflected script with ribbon-like ornamental strokes referencing Argentine filete motifs.
description: Festival Script continues the Koziupa/Paul deco-script line established by Aranjuez, Bellas Artes, Heraldica and Tanguera, this time with a more geometric sensibility and strong bilinear contrast. Nearly every letterform carries multiple alternates, running from minimal to exuberant, positioning it for modern luxury branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Festival Script's ribbon-like strokes as evoking Argentine filete motifs, combining bilinear contrast with ornamental swashes.

name: Fixture
classification_notes: A 72-style grotesque referencing wood-letterpress and poster type of the late nineteenth century, built as a functional workhorse across four widths.
summary: A 72-style grotesque workhorse spanning four widths and nine weights, referencing late nineteenth-century wood letterpress type.
description: Fixture takes on the plentiful grotesque offerings of Victorian-era typefaces and poster type, running from Ultra Compressed to Expanded in nine weights each with matching italics. It was built with enough functional flexibility to work from subtle magazine layout and film credits through to billboard-scale packaging drama, and now includes a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Fixture a massive 72-font take on the plentiful late nineteenth-century Grotesk genre, built as a workhorse for multiple environments.

name: Frambuesa
classification_notes: A half-humanist, half-geometric sans that shares its structure and proportions with the serif Elisetta, its 'older sister'.
summary: A humanist/geometric hybrid sans across seven weights, sharing its proportions with the serif Elisetta.
description: Frambuesa merges decorative curves with straight lines, balancing organic and geometric in a solid, somewhat nostalgic design. Structure and proportions come directly from Elisetta, and seven carefully adjusted weights keep the transitions between them smooth for both text and large titles.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos names Frambuesa for designer Lu Ronderos's childhood, a sweet tribute honouring a family fruit gift, in a font that reveals its family genetics from Elisetta.

name: Franqueline Slab
classification_notes: Inspired by late nineteenth-century Egyptian slab serifs, spanning a full weight range with a slanted rather than true italic.
summary: A nine-weight Egyptian-inspired slab designed by Estudio Vástago, from delicately refined to boldly eye-catching.
description: Franqueline Slab takes its cue from the timeless Egyptian slab serifs of the late nineteenth century, its delicate strokes and sophisticated endings striking a balance between contemporary edge and traditional charm. The full weight axis suits captivating headlines as well as more restrained editorial settings.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Franqueline Slab elegantly inspired by the timeless Egyptian fonts of the late nineteenth century, distributed by Sudtipos and designed by Estudio Vástago.

name: French Bulldog
classification_notes: A deliberately unpredictable, chaos-driven casual handwriting script rather than a formal or brush-consistent style.
summary: A spontaneous casual-hand script celebrating small, unnoticed everyday moments.
description: French Bulldog creates spontaneity from chaos, its different shapes working randomly to swing between finesse and coarseness like a casual hand trying to follow rules with unpredictable results. It reads versatile and fresh, friendly and relaxed.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos made French Bulldog to celebrate the unnoticed precious little moments, a font that flows in the moment.

name: Frigga
classification_notes: Rooted in the Baroque Dutch tradition of text typefaces and northern European letterforms, spanning 20 styles named after the Norse goddess Frigga.
summary: A Baroque Dutch text serif in 20 styles, named for the Norse goddess Frigga, built for both long-form text and expressive display.
description: Frigga balances a solid historic structure with a refreshing repertoire of organic forms, reading comfortable and close in long text settings but exuberant and detailed in headlines. Each style carries more than a thousand glyphs, with alternates, ornaments, borders and both old-style and tabular figures, and the family includes a variable version.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Frigga beautiful, timeless, lush, elegant and smooth like nordic mead, fully equipped for the wildest editorial needs.

name: Fulgora
classification_notes: Blends late-medieval Bâtarde and Civilité blackletter with Kannada, Sinhala, Celtic uncial and Mexican vernacular script influences, offered in two ink-width variants.
summary: A calligraphic blackletter blending Bâtarde and Civilité with Celtic uncials and Mexican vernacular scripts, in Blanca and Negra weights.
description: Fulgora was drawn straight from pen to paper as a personal calligraphic style before being vectorised and digitally assembled, keeping its natural, imperfect, hand-finished character intact. Its Blanca and Negra variants use different nib widths to shift the mood from lighter to heavier.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Fulgora a calligraphic typography or typographic calligraphy, aiming for an utterly calligraphic outcome with a natural, imperfect manual finish.

name: Galgo Script
classification_notes: Mixes elegant brush calligraphy with rough, weathered scrawl, named for the speed of the Spanish Greyhound breed.
summary: A rough-yet-elegant brush script named for the Spanish Greyhound, mixing calligraphy with speedy scrawl.
description: Galgo Script suits logomarks, titles and single sentences as well as longer artistic writing passages, built specifically to answer demand for this kind of "rush brush" style.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos likens Galgo Script to the Galgo greyhound, a mix of elegant brush calligraphy and the rough, weathered strokes of speedy scrawl.

name: Geminian
classification_notes: A themed set of Caps, Script and Signs fonts built around an astrological Gemini concept, rather than a single unified letterform system.
summary: An astrology-themed lettering set of Caps, Script and Signs fonts, celebrating Gemini's associations with communication.
description: Geminian was developed over a long period from a theoretical idea into a full creative set, its multiple fonts intended as a medium for carrying different messages. The set includes Roman and Bold caps alongside a companion script and astrological signs, suited to stationery and scrapbooking work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Geminian as reviving the main features of the Gemini sign, associated with thoughts, creativity and communication.

name: Gintona Sans
subcategory: grotesque companion to a slab serif
classification_notes: A sans companion to Gintona Slab, shedding the slab's sturdy serifs while keeping its balanced proportions and energetic character.
summary: A modern, versatile grotesque in eight weights, sharing the Gintona family's energy while shedding its slab serifs.
description: Gintona Sans sheds the sturdy serifs of Gintona Slab in favour of fluidity, while keeping the family's balanced proportions and dynamic feel. Eight weights and a variable version make it work equally for immersive text, bold headlines and graphic compositions.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Gintona Sans as carrying the distinctive spirit of the Gintona family, adapting easily to editorial, branding and digital design.

name: Gintona Slab
classification_notes: A slab serif with thick serifs and pronounced ink traps used as a stylistic device, plus diagonal terminals that give it organic warmth.
summary: A sturdy slab serif with pronounced ink traps and diagonal terminals, spanning eight weights plus a variable font.
description: Gintona combines thick serifs and ink traps as a deliberate stylistic resource, its diagonal terminals and organic shapes giving it a warm, dynamic presence. It runs from delicately refined to bold and heavy across eight weights, suited to editorial work, logos, packaging and advertising.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Gintona a sturdy, fresh and modern typeface that adds a distinctive touch to editorial, logo and packaging projects.

name: Glodok
classification_notes: A single-weight, bold retro-inspired display face named after Jakarta's oldest Chinatown district.
summary: A bold, single-weight retro display face named after Jakarta's oldest and largest Chinatown district.
description: Glodok is heavy and eye-catching but blends well within a layout, balancing formal and playful in equal measure. The designer drew inspiration directly from Jakarta's historic Glodok neighbourhood.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos names Glodok for the oldest Chinatown in Jakarta, also considered the biggest in Indonesia, the place the designer drew inspiration from.

name: Gothalian
classification_notes: Rooted in Henry Brehmer's 1890s metal type for George Bruce's Son & Co, revived with Victorian ironwork influence across a full variable weight range.
summary: A Victorian-rooted blackletter revived from Henry Brehmer's 1890s metal type, spanning nine weights and three widths.
description: Gothalian extrapolates the essence of Henry Brehmer's 1890s type for George Bruce's Son & Co, adding the ornate ironwork character of the late nineteenth century. It comes as a flexible variable font or nine static styles with italics, giving it a sophisticated, faintly dark aura for tattoo and gothic branding work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Gothalian as reviving vintage source material with the ornate ironwork of the late nineteenth century for a sophisticated, attractive look.

name: Grappa
classification_notes: Based on Morris Fuller Benton's classic Invitation typeface, distinguished by unique triangular serifs across a full nine-weight range.
summary: A nine-weight serif revival of Morris Fuller Benton's Invitation typeface, marked out by distinctive triangular serifs.
description: Grappa is named for the Italian spirit, both typeface and drink sharing a sense of craft and sensory character. It builds on Benton's Invitation with unique triangle serifs, alternates and swash characters, offered as nine static weights plus a variable font.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos introduces Grappa as based on the classic Invitation typeface by Morris Fuller Benton, featuring unique triangle serifs that give it a distinct edge.

name: Gratitude Script
classification_notes: A hand-drawn celebratory script sold across Pro and Smooth variants with matching ornament and word sets rather than a weight ladder.
summary: A hand-drawn celebratory script with companion ornament and word sets, built for greetings and invitation work.
description: Gratitude Script comes in regular and Smooth variants, each paired with an ornaments set and a set of pre-built words, for greeting cards, invitations and stationery. It reads as deeply personal, drawing on themes of appreciation and everyday beauty.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Gratitude Script as a celebratory font born from an appreciation for the beauty found in art, nature and loving relationships.

name: Griff Mono
classification_notes: A monospaced typeface built from calligraphic construction rationalised onto a fixed-width grid, rather than a typewriter or coding-first mono design.
summary: A calligraphically-constructed monospace with spiky, assertive curves, in Regular and bolder Heavy weights.
description: Griff Mono rationalises calligraphic construction within a fixed monospaced grid, its stinging, claw-like curves bringing energy to both footnotes and headlines. It stays crisp and clear at small sizes while revealing a strong personality when scaled up.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Griff Mono as holding its edge and demanding attention across compact footnotes, bold headlines and singular logotypes, no compromises.

name: Grover
classification_notes: Joins basic European gothic sans structure from the late nineteenth century with a 1960s American rounded style, named after jazz musician Grover Washington Jr.
summary: A clear, friendly rounded sans joining nineteenth-century European gothic structure with a 1960s American rounded style.
description: Grover is geometrically constructed yet very human in appearance, named after jazz saxophonist Grover Washington Jr. True italics and small caps sit alongside a matching slab-serif sibling, Grover Slab, for combined display versatility.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Grover as joining the basic European gothic of the late nineteenth century with the rounded style found in 1960s America.

name: Grover Slab
classification_notes: The slab-serif sibling to Grover, sharing its geometric-yet-human construction and rounded 1960s American character.
summary: A clear, friendly rounded slab serif, the slab-serif sibling to Grover.
description: Grover Slab carries the same clear, friendly geometric construction as its sans sibling Grover, adding slab serifs for a sturdier presence. True italics and small caps give it the same display versatility.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos presents Grover Slab as sharing Grover's aim to join nineteenth-century European gothic structure with a 1960s American rounded style, this time as a slab.

name: Habano ST
classification_notes: An elegantly flowing bold script blending art deco style with pop-culture lettering, with contrasting classy lowercase and playfully round capitals.
summary: An elegantly flowing bold script mixing art deco style with playful pop-culture lettering.
description: Habano's classy, obedient lowercase contrasts with round, memorable majuscules and figures, turning simple words into distinctive images. It works well for packaging and logo work looking for a soft, lasting touch.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Habano an elegantly flowing bold script taking roots in both art deco style and pop-culture lettering.

name: Heartline
classification_notes: A monolinear handwriting-inspired display face rather than a broad-nib calligraphic script, built as a variable font from Extra Light to Bold.
summary: A monolinear, handwriting-inspired display script with flowing swashes, built as a variable font from Extra Light to Bold.
description: Heartline is designed for expressive display use in headlines and short texts, its flowing swashes and entangled decorative elements adding movement to the core letterforms. A wide Pan-European Latin range and a variable font version give it flexibility across stationery and fashion branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Heartline shines wherever calligraphy has a voice, in stationery design, fashion branding, packaging and beyond.

name: Hejira
