classification_notes: Four distinct, deliberately unrelated-looking styles (a spiky thin serif, an extreme experimental sibling, a calligraphic sans, and a quirky fat face) unified by a shared underlying system rather than a conventional weight ramp.
summary: An atypical four-style serif system named for rupture, each style with its own distinct, deliberately unconventional personality.
description: Hejira means "rupture", the guiding idea being to escape convention with an unusual, fresh approach. Its four styles range from a thin, spiky serif and an extreme titling sibling on the same skeleton to an odd sans that mimics a calligraphic pen and a quirky fat face, all built to work together despite their differences.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Hejira's four styles as atypical, each with its own distinct personality yet feeling part of the same system.

name: Henderson Sans
subcategory: grotesque companion to a slab serif
classification_notes: A sans built by stripping the serifs from Henderson Slab, keeping glyph-for-glyph consistency with its slab sibling rather than a separately-conceived design.
summary: A sleek, serifless counterpart to Henderson Slab, sharing glyph-for-glyph consistency across seven weights plus italics.
description: Henderson Sans came from stripping the serifs off Henderson Slab, a deliberate evolution that keeps the craftsmanship of its predecessor in a more modern form. Alternates and swashes carry over from the slab version, giving designers a cohesive duo to work with.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Henderson Sans a contemporary interpretation that confidently asserts its own identity while mirroring the sophistication of Henderson Slab.

name: Henderson Slab
classification_notes: Rooted in bold caps drawn by Albert Du Bois for the 1906 Henderson Sign Painter book, developed into a full geometric slab-serif family.
summary: A geometric slab serif rooted in Albert Du Bois's 1906 Henderson Sign Painter capitals, now a family of seven weights plus italics.
description: Henderson Slab began with a few bold caps from a 1906 sign-painting manual, growing from majuscules into a full lowercase, six more weights and italics over the course of its development. It covers nearly the entire range of the slab-serif genre through its weight axis, with extended Latin language support.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Henderson Slab to Albert Du Bois's bold caps for the 1906 Henderson Sign Painter book, exploring how sign painters approached slabs after the industrial revolution.

name: Heraldica Script
classification_notes: Combines classic thin-and-thick script strokes with thin-only counterpart strokes and overlaid flourishes for a particularly ornamented, deluxe effect.
summary: One of the foundry's most ornamented scripts, combining thick-and-thin strokes with overlaid flourishes for a deluxe finish.
description: Heraldica conjoins classic thin-and-thick script treatment with thin-only counterpart strokes, then adds a varied complement of overlaid flourishes for extra class. Multiple alternates and ending forms make it suitable for monograms, logos, jewelry packaging and book covers.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Heraldica one of Koziupa and Paul's most expressive ornamented scripts, attaining the very definition of deluxe.

name: Herencia
classification_notes: A sophisticated rough calligraphic script designed specifically for packaging and stationery use.
summary: A beautiful, sophisticated rough calligraphic script built for packaging and stationery.
description: Herencia (Spanish for heritage) carries an antique, textured calligraphic quality suited to labels and stationery that want a handmade sense of history.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Herencia a beautiful and sophisticated rough calligraphy specially designed for packaging and stationery.

name: Herr Von Muellerhoff Pro
classification_notes: Another entry in the Bluemlein Script Collection, assembled from collaged historic hand-letterer signatures rather than a single calligrapher's hand.
summary: A Bluemlein Script Collection revival named for an invented calligrapher persona from 1930s-40s New York.
description: Herr Von Muellerhoff Pro belongs to the same Bluemlein Script Collection as Dr Carbfred and Dr Sugiyama, built from collaged historic hand-lettering signatures and given a fictitious name for its original Higgins Ink catalogue feature. Sudtipos brought it into a modern digital format for wedding and stationery work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos revives another of the Charles Bluemlein scripts, a reminder of the heady days when about 200 professional hand letterers worked in New York City.

name: Hipster Script
classification_notes: An attempt to get digital type to emulate continuous brush painting, casual in contrast rather than the high seriousness of a copperplate script.
summary: A brush-emulating script uniting spontaneous post-war ad lettering with current illustration trends, winner of a Type Directors Club Judge's Choice award.
description: Hipster Script tries to articulate brush lettering digitally, continuing the computerised commercial-lettering approach begun with Feel Script but with more casual contrast. Extensive swashes, alternates and ligatures, including unusual apostrophe ligatures, keep the interplay between the brush's extreme widths faithful to hand movement.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Hipster Script as balancing the spontaneity of post-war ad lettering with current illustration and design trends.

name: Hopfen
classification_notes: Brings Bentele's German lettering, which also inspired Semilla and Bowling Script, into a five-weight display family rather than a single style.
summary: A five-weight display face reviving Bentele's German lettering for brewery and packaging use.
description: Hopfen (German for hops) brings back Bentele's lettering, the same source that inspired Semilla and Bowling Script, in a more versatile multi-weight form. Swashes, endings and alternates run through all five weights, and a variable version is included with the complete set.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos imagines Hopfen used from breweries to book covers, from packaging to movie posters, though it leaves the better use to its customers.

name: Horizontes
classification_notes: A personal experimental calligraphy project balancing spontaneity and elegance, in two weights for large and small formats.
summary: A relaxed, energetic monoline script inspired by a coastal horizon, in two weights for large and small formats.
description: Horizontes was born from Panco Sassano's personal experimental calligraphy project, seeking a balance between spontaneity, elegance and beauty. Wide-ranging ligatures, initial letters and flourishes suit invitations, labels and poetry that want warmth without excess formality.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces Horizontes to the blue line of the horizon from the city where designer Panco Sassano was born.

name: Hot Salsa
classification_notes: Mixes classic sign-painting brush lettering with fast, gestural graffiti tags, retraced by hand from brush-pen originals for consistent structure.
summary: A brush-pen calligraphic script mixing casual sign-painting lettering with fast, gestural graffiti tags.
description: Hot Salsa started with a brush pen and a lot of paper, later re-traced onto tracing paper to keep the handmade feeling while making the structure consistent enough for reliable performance. Numerous swashes, alternates and ligatures let it swing from sober to flirty.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Hot Salsa as inspired by classic brush letters from casual sign-painting mixed with the fast, gestural tags found on walls worldwide.

name: Identa
classification_notes: A pragmatic, functionality-first sans built specifically for identity design, spanning White through Vantablack weights with true italics.
summary: A workhorse identity-design sans running from White to Vantablack, built for reliability across short identifiers and long text.
description: Identa seeks a dialogue between neutrality and contemporaneity, translating corporate and humanist ideals into an accessible, well-founded sans. Its clean forms and x-height work for both short identifiers and long-form text, with eight styles each carrying a matching italic.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Identa as an all-terrain, workhorse typeface that solves any type of content with efficiency, intelligence and professionalism.

name: Inglesa
classification_notes: The Spanish term for copperplate calligraphy, developed into its own typographic personality across six weights with a companion Roman caps set.
summary: A copperplate-derived script in six weights from skinny monolinear to elegant black, with a companion Roman caps set.
description: Inglesa (Spanish for the English style, referring to copperplate calligraphy) developed its own typographic personality beyond its historic starting point. Its Script and Caps sets share the same weight range, giving it a strong English spirit with a fresh Latin spice and a large stock of alternates, endings and swashes.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Inglesa the perfect combination for elegant design, transmitting a strong English spirit with a fresh Latin spice.

name: Inlove
classification_notes: A high-contrast geometric display face by a designer whose work was influential enough to be featured at New York's Herb Lubalin Exhibition.
summary: A high-contrast geometric display face by Ariel Di Lisio, whose work was shown at New York's Herb Lubalin Exhibition.
description: Inlove is a modern take on Di Lisio's passion for geometric, heavily contrasted typefaces, suited to magazines, posters and flyers. Its strong influence saw the designer invited to be part of the 2009 Herb Lubalin Exhibition in New York.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Inlove a modern take of Ariel Di Lisio's passion for geometric and very contrasted typefaces.

name: Inoxida
classification_notes: A softer, more graceful reworking of Oxida's rough letter construction, with a smoother size relationship between upper and lowercase.
summary: A softer, more graceful sister to Oxida, reworked for food packaging that calls for sophisticated script lettering.
description: Inoxida is not simply a smoothed-out Oxida, but a complete reworking of its letter construction with a gentler size relationship between cases. It suits food packaging that wants elegance rather than Oxida's rougher edge.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Inoxida Oxida's softer and more graceful sister, fitting the bill for food packaging that benefits from sophisticated script lettering.

name: Integra
classification_notes: Emerges from the border between sans and serif, inspired by unserifed letterforms incised at Santa Croce church and Stourhead's neoclassical grotto inscriptions.
summary: A sans/serif hybrid inspired by fifteenth-century incised ledger tombs and eighteenth-century grotto inscriptions.
description: Integra integrates sans and serif in one sleek, elegant anatomy, its flared terminals and near-absent straight lines borrowed from historic incised lettering at Santa Croce and Stourhead. Audacious shapes on letters like L, E and X give it a futuristic, Latin American-flavoured twist across several weights and italic styles.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Integra as emerging from the hazy border that divides sans from serif, aiming to integrate both styles in a cool, contemporary fashion.

name: Isla
classification_notes: A digitisation of Eugène Grasset's 1898 poster italic, its irregular quality giving it an older, historical flavour than a conventional transitional italic.
summary: A digitisation of Eugène Grasset's 1898 poster italic, its irregular quality lending an older, historical flavour.
description: Isla revives an italic Swiss designer Eugène Grasset drew in 1898 for two of his posters, an irregular design that reads as considerably older than its date. A wealth of ligatures and alternates suit map-related design and historical publications, maintaining respect for its original flavour.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos digitised Isla with the utmost respect for its historical flavour, drawn from one of Eugène Grasset's rarely mentioned typographic treasures.

name: Jugo Script
classification_notes: A near-parody of soft, speedy late-1980s and early-1990s display scripts, with a mischievous wink at Oz Cooper's lens-blurred film types.
summary: A near-parody of soft, speedy late-1980s display scripts, with a mischievous nod to Oz Cooper's lens-blurred film types.
description: Jugo Script's uppercase and figures show Koziupa's distinctive sense of letterform and proportion, while the lowercase runs as an eccentric single-stroke exercise with quick wrist bends and hurried exits. Its softness and internal rhythm make it a natural for comfort food packaging.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Jugo Script's softness and internal call-and-answer structure as a natural for comfort food packaging, especially the sweet stuff.

name: Kautiva Pro
subcategory: modern sans with unicase and multi-script support
classification_notes: A middle ground between geometric and humanist sans, distinguished by unicase variations and support for Cyrillic and Greek alongside Latin.
summary: A wide-ranging modern sans offering a refreshing middle ground between geometric and humanist design, with Cyrillic and Greek support.
description: Kautiva includes true italics, small caps and unicase variations, built to be efficient in both text and display environments. The OpenType Pro family adds proportional and tabular figures and complete support across Latin, Cyrillic and Greek scripts.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Kautiva as a refreshing middle ground between serious geometric and overly humanistic design.

name: Kewl Script
classification_notes: A heavier, playful script with a South American sign-letterer's twist, conceived alongside the Bluemlein revivals before being finished separately.
summary: A heavier, playful script with a South American sign-letterer's twist, related in spirit to Candy Script and Whomp.
description: Kewl emerged while finishing Mrs Blackfort, the first of the Bluemlein fonts, when some letters began morphing differently in the designer's mind. The idea seeped partly into Candy Script and Whomp before Kewl itself was finished, and it now suits food packaging, book and music covers, magazines and window displays.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Kewl ideal for food packaging, book and music covers, magazines and window splashes.

name: Kilo
classification_notes: A fast-feeling display script that switches between connected and freestyle letterforms, with edgy capitals and expressive vowels.
summary: A fast-feeling display script with edgy capitals and expressive vowels, switching between connected and freestyle forms.
description: Kilo has edgy caps built to keep it together at high velocities, with vowels that grin and salute as they go by. Plenty of alternates give it flexibility for branding and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Kilo flows like the liquid its name suggests, sometimes connected and sometimes freestyle.

name: Koziupack
classification_notes: A wild, curled brush script with sharp-focus ascenders and descenders, built for food and drink product labelling.
summary: A wild but sharply-focused curled brush script built for food and drink product labels.
description: Koziupack pairs curled ascenders and descenders with swashy, care-free caps and unique figures, a strong choice for signage and magazine advertisements alongside packaging. It also stands out well knocked out of a dark background.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Koziupack the ideal choice of font for food and drink product labels, signage and magazine advertisements.

name: Kozmetica
classification_notes: A soft, fluid script with art deco ornamentation concentrated in the lowercase, built for packaging design.
summary: A soft, warm script with art deco lowercase ornamentation, built for elegant packaging design.
description: Kozmetica's fluid strokes make for a comfortable, classy delivery, with plentiful alternates focusing on the degree of lowercase ornamentation. Settings can stay simple or swash out into swirling hairlines depending on the mood.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Kozmetica new original elegance with just enough ornamentation to evoke the rich days of art deco, ideal for packaging design.

name: Kukulkan
classification_notes: Reworks ancient Roman letter structure with fantastical, pre-Hispanic Mayan-inspired details, built for continuous text despite its decorative origins.
summary: A Roman-letter serif infused with pre-Hispanic Mayan idealisation, built for legible continuous text across nine weights.
description: Kukulkan unravels structural possibilities within ancient Roman letters and fantastical styles, its darker weights carrying the most pronounced Mayan cultural nuance. Sturdy, assured strokes keep it working well as continuous text, and it is available as a variable font alongside its nine static weights.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Kukulkan as infused with subtle elements that evoke a pre-Hispanic idealization of Mayan culture, most notable in its darker iterations.

name: Kukulkan Sans
classification_notes: The sans counterpart to Kukulkan, sharing its typographic ductus, optical adjustments and spacing while adopting contemporary sans-serif standards.
summary: The sans counterpart to Kukulkan, translating its ancient Roman and Mayan-inflected structure into contemporary sans-serif standards.
description: Kukulkan Sans stays intrinsically linked to its serif predecessor in ductus, optical adjustment and spacing, its legibility integrating the same pre-Hispanic Mayan idealisation particularly visible in darker variants. Each of its 18 styles includes swash designs matching its serif counterpart, adding a humanistic touch to the sans structure.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Kukulkan Sans as intrinsically linked to its predecessor, blending ancient Roman letters, fantastical charm and contemporary sans-serif standards.

name: KWINC Grotesk
classification_notes: Inspired by vernacular dimensional letters found in US home improvement stores, pairing an expressive uppercase with an old-style lowercase across nine weights.
summary: A playful, functional grotesque from New York studio Karlssonwilker, inspired by vernacular dimensional letters found in home improvement stores.
description: KWINC Grotesk is the first collaboration between Karlssonwilker, the acclaimed New York design studio founded in 2000, and Sudtipos. Its strikingly expressive uppercase pairs with an old-style lowercase, running to nine weights with italics and a variable version.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls KWINC Grotesk a reflection of Karlssonwilker's bold, dynamic spirit, born from long creative conversations between Hjalti Karlsson, Jan Wilker and Ale Paul.

name: La Portenia
designer: Diego Giaccone, Angel Koziupa, Alejandro Paul
classification_notes: Pays homage to early twentieth-century show-card writers, offered in two variants (a formal Recoleta and a showier, flourished Boca) rather than a weight ladder.
summary: A show-card lettering script in two Buenos Aires-flavoured variants, the formal Recoleta and the showier, flourished Boca.
description: La Portenia pays homage to the spirit of early twentieth-century show-card writers and type designers. De Recoleta is slightly more formal and polite, while de la Boca has longer, more extravagant flourishes and wider interletter space, reminiscent of hand-painted signs found around Buenos Aires.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes La Portenia's two variants as ranging from the formal Recoleta district to the showier signs of La Boca.

name: La Taquería
classification_notes: A chalkboard-art-inspired hand-lettering toolkit sold as four related styles (Bold, Informal, Inline, Script) rather than a weight ramp.
summary: A chalkboard-inspired hand-lettering toolkit of four styles built for menus and food branding.
description: La Taquería mixes bold, informal, inline and script styles into one DIY-flavoured set, aimed at menu boards and casual food branding. Its wild, hand-lettered character suits chalkboard art and scrapbook-style packaging alike.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos positions La Taquería as a chalkboard-art hand-lettering set for bars, menus and food branding.

name: Lady Dodo
classification_notes: A systematised yet personal pointed-nib script inspired by Maurice Maeterlinck's nature writing, following on from its sister font Lady René, with a companion patterns set.
summary: A systematised yet personal pointed-nib script inspired by Maurice Maeterlinck's nature writing, sister to Lady René.
description: Lady Dodó grew from passages of Maeterlinck's "Life and Flowers" and reflection on the spontaneous, sometimes ink-stained flow of pen on paper. It follows its ancestor Lady René in using OpenType to offer both a systematised and a personalised writing font, with a large number of alternates for upper and lower case.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Lady Dodó as born from poetic observation of nature, proposing a font that is both systematized and personalized, friendly and challenging.

name: Lady René
classification_notes: A script treating the written word as illustration and narration, built by an editorial designer with a background in books and CD sleeves rather than a pure calligrapher.
summary: An illustrative, narrative script from a designer who treats the written word as drawing rather than pure calligraphy.
description: Lady René comes from designer Laura Varsky's fifteen years working on editorial pieces, mostly books and CD sleeves, where typography always sat at the centre of her research. The font calls in the written word to illustrate and narrate, embodying both a search for spotless text and something more daring.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Lady René as work from a graphic designer and Typography professor whose obsessions embody the search for both a perfect and a provoking text.

name: Lagarto
classification_notes: Digitises a colonial-era manuscript by scribe Luis Lagarto, preserving three distinct hands (Roman roundhand, ornate Italic, playful small caps) within one family.
summary: A digital revival of a colonial Mexican manuscript by scribe Luis Lagarto, preserving three distinct historic hands.
description: Lagarto translates an eccentric, late-1500s manuscript found by editorial publisher Blacamán Ediciones into a digital family, keeping the baroque Roman roundhand, ornate Italic and playful small caps of the original scribe. Since the manuscript had no numerals or modern punctuation, part of the work involved inferring these from the existing hands.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Lagarto as translating an incredible and stunningly original colonial manuscript, featuring three different hands by the scribe, into digital type.

name: Landa
classification_notes: Inspired by fifteenth-century Venetian lettering, reworked with an expressionist, natural-textured touch referencing both Nicolas Jenson and Oldřich Menhart.
summary: An expressionist revival of fifteenth-century Venetian lettering, a rendez-vous between Nicolas Jenson, Oldřich Menhart and nature itself.
description: Landa gives Venetian lettering a modern, expressionist touch, its letters carrying the texture of tree trunks and branches from fertile splendour to dried-out frailty. Five weights with italics and small caps suit books, newspapers and corporate editorial work that wants imperfection and soul.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Landa a glimpse from the cutting edge into the past, connecting with the imperfect and controlled impurity that is nature.

name: Latinaires Pro
classification_notes: An updated version of one of the first Sudtipos typefaces, expanded with more weights and small caps for modern brand and editorial use.
summary: A legible corporate text sans, updated from one of the foundry's earliest typefaces with more weights and small caps.
description: Latinaires Pro now covers more Latin languages than its original release, with additional weights and small caps aimed at modern brand communication. It suits both headline and body-text use in editorial and corporate settings.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Latinaires Pro as specially designed for modern brand communication and editorial use.

name: Lombriz
classification_notes: A heavy yet casual, semi-connected script bridging packaging, signage and sporting lettering conventions from the 1950s.
summary: A heavy but casual semi-connected 1950s-flavoured script bridging packaging, signage and sports lettering.
description: Lombriz feels friendlier, more readable and more real than most scripts of its kind, its capital letters thickening while the lowercase flows like casual brush-drawn writing. More than 50 alternates and custom ligatures sit inside the OpenType version.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Lombriz as attempting to bridge the gap between different kinds of typography, including packaging, signage and sporting.

name: Looking Flowers
classification_notes: An informal pointed-nib script inspired by Lima's Miraflores district, sold with companion Caps, Deco and Pro variants rather than a weight ladder.
summary: An informal, wide-ranging pointed-nib script by Peruvian lettering artist Lunol, inspired by Lima's Miraflores district.
description: Looking Flowers (Mirando las flores) is Lunol's first typeface, designed in collaboration with Alejandro Paul, with many alternates, swashes and ligatures alongside small caps and ornaments. It covers an expansive range of Latin languages, intended for stationery, menus and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos introduces Lunol as a fresh representative of a new generation of South American lettering artists, inspired by Lima's upscale Miraflores district.

name: Lumbrance Sans
classification_notes: Distinguished by pronounced corners and slightly raised horizontal strokes, blending irreverence with formality across a full weight and width range.
summary: An angular, sharp-cornered contemporary sans balancing irreverence with formality across condensed, regular and expanded widths.
description: Lumbrance Sans incorporates distinctive pronounced corners and slightly raised horizontal strokes for a personality-rich but still balanced design. Its variable format invites playful compositions across a weight range the foundry describes as diverse as human emotions.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Lumbrance Sans a typeface that reflects a deep connection with typographic design, combining personality and balance between traditional and contemporary styles.

name: Lynda
classification_notes: A post-modern monoline rounded sans built for club flyers and fashion publications rather than corporate or editorial text use.
summary: A post-modern monoline rounded sans built for club flyers, music covers and fashion publications.
description: Lynda keeps a consistent monoline rounded structure throughout, with a distinctly industrial, futuristic tone suited to nightlife and fashion graphics.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Lynda a post-modern, monoline rounded sans ideal for club flyers, music covers and fashion publications.

name: Machete
classification_notes: A heavy, in-your-face woodcut-style display face described as Bayoneta's overfed distant cousin, built for maximum bulk rather than delicacy.
summary: A hulky, in-your-face woodcut-style display face, Bayoneta's overfed distant cousin.
description: Machete is built big and full of humour, suited to comfort-food packaging, road-trip comedy posters and anywhere a large, loud alphabet is called for.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Machete doesn't text, it roars.

name: Magari
classification_notes: Partially inspired by mid-nineteenth-century German condensed serifs with Italian Didone connections, running from ultra-compressed thin to extended black.
summary: A jazzy, Didone-influenced display serif running from ultra-compressed thin to extended black across nine weights.
description: Magari extrapolates mid-nineteenth-century German condensed serif ideas, with a clear Italian Didone connection, into a unique variable font or nine specific weights. Three kinds of lowercase endings and two swash sets for the capitals let it play across advertising, packaging and editorial design.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos names Magari after a lovely Italian expression, describing the font as jazzy and able to assure great impact whether thin and tall or big and bold.

name: Malambo
classification_notes: A rustic, energetic script named for the traditional Argentine gaucho dance, built with a jittery, cheekily imperfect brush character.
summary: A rustic, energetic script named after Malambo, the traditional Argentine gaucho dance.
description: Malambo is full of energy and cheeky mischief, its jittery brush character carrying the passion of the gaucho dance it's named for. It suits craft, artisanal and folk-themed branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Malambo full of energy and cheeky mischief, a typeface that is all about dancing.

name: Malbeck
classification_notes: An elegant, unique script with a large alternates set, built for OpenType-aware playful typographic treatments.
summary: An elegant, unique script with a large alternates set for playful typographic treatments.
description: Malbeck opens up very playful typographic possibilities through its large selection of alternate characters, best used in OpenType-aware applications.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Malbeck a script which is both as elegant as it is unique.

name: Mama Script
classification_notes: Began as an experiment in vertical calligraphy, drawing on swashy handwriting and lettering rather than a single calligraphic model.
summary: A swashy handwriting script that began as an experiment in vertical calligraphy.
description: Mama Script draws on multiple sources from casual handwriting and signage to renowned calligraphers, coming with a full set of alternates and ligatures for precise display use, balancing hand and machine.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Mama Script likes to stand out everywhere it appears, simulating a balance between the hand and the machine.

name: Maquina
classification_notes: Based on illustrator Leandro Castelao's own machinery and cable-themed lettering, sold as both a colour font and a black-and-white OTF.
summary: An industrial, machinery-themed colour font built from illustrator Leandro Castelao's lettering.
description: Máquina plays with cables and geometry to create an intricate but clean, controlled-chaos display face, elegant with playful details. It ships as CMYK and RGB colour-font palettes alongside a standard black-and-white OTF.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Máquina as machinery, cables and geometry come together as its playground, complex but playful, elegant with fun little details.

name: Marti Sans
classification_notes: A contrast sans with sturdy touches reminiscent of flat-nib calligraphic strokes, with a reduced ascender height that improves readability.
summary: A contrast sans with flat-nib calligraphic touches, designed by Estudio Vástago with a reduced ascender height for readability.
description: Marti Sans reinterprets classic sans-serif contrast with authentic flat-nib calligraphic strokes, its heavier weights showing bold slant and distorted dots while lighter weights keep the same details more subtle. A balanced width supports harmonious composition across both body text and headlines.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Marti Sans a design statement recommended for websites, branding and any project seeking refined elegance.

name: Marzo
classification_notes: A monoline, minimalist sans pushing its forms toward a state of natural purity rather than a workhorse text design.
summary: A monoline, minimalist sans pushing its forms toward natural purity and elegance.
description: Marzo keeps a single stroke weight throughout, its geometric restraint aimed squarely at clean, modern minimalism.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Marzo a monoline, minimalist, modern typeface that tries to take its forms to a state of natural purity, definitively elegant.

name: Mathilde
classification_notes: Inspired by floral cyanotype experiments, with thorny serifs and droplet-shaped stroke ends that give it an organic, growing quality.
summary: A thorny-serifed display serif inspired by floral cyanotype experiments, across six weights with matching italics.
description: Mathilde combines sharp, small elements with graceful, flowing shapes, its convex and concave lines and pointed droplet-shaped stroke ends drawing a connection to a literary rose. It works equally for organic, growing headlines and harmonious continuous text.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos says Mathilde infuses editorial design, branding or packaging with an idyllic and organic message.

name: Mati
classification_notes: Digitises a complete hand-drawn alphabet made by the designer's eleven-year-old son, a genuinely childlike, grungy hand-lettering style.
summary: A grungy, childlike hand-lettering display face digitised from a complete alphabet drawn by the designer's eleven-year-old son.
description: Mati was a Father's Day present, a complete alphabet drawn on a sheet of A4 paper by Matías, Alejandro Paul's son, later digitised in full. It suits scrapbooking, casual branding and anything wanting a genuinely handmade, youthful feel.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Mati's origin as a handmade Father's Day present, a complete alphabet, grungy, childish and sweeter than a ton of honey.

name: Matogrosso Script
classification_notes: A rough script built around discovery and the outdoors, using alternate lowercase characters to generate natural, uneven texture.
summary: A rough, expressive script well suited to wine labels, organic food packaging and old maps.
description: Matogrosso's OpenType programming combines several alternate lowercase characters to generate a perfectly fit, natural texture. Its expressive urge toward discovery suits designs relating to outdoor activity and rugged travel.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Matogrosso another rough script from the Argentine calligraphy team of Koziupa and Paul.

name: ME Plastic
classification_notes: Digitises a found set of plastic toy-store stencil letters rather than a drawn design, keeping a bold connected set alongside individual characters.
summary: A vernacular stencil display face digitised from a found set of plastic toy alphabet letters.
description: ME Plastic began as a plastic alphabet toy discovered in a London shop, later digitised by Mario Eskenazi and his daughter Gabriela. It features a bold set of connected letters alongside individual characters, suited to book covers and cultural posters that want a casual, vernacular personality.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos traces ME Plastic to a set of plastic alphabet letters found in a London toy store, a serendipitous discovery that sparked a collection and eventually a font.

name: Merengue Script
classification_notes: Signs inspired by brush-pen calligraphy but drawn or literally illustrated rather than following traditional calligraphic construction, sold in a Basic tier alongside the full version.
summary: An illustrated brush-pen script with weight and presence at large formats, still efficient at small sizes.
description: Merengue Script's signs are inspired by brush-pen calligraphy but drawn and illustrated rather than tied to traditional calligraphy or text typography. Designed with weight and presence for big formats while staying efficient for brief small-format texts, it suits packaging and grocery branding.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Merengue Script as an unusual font with personality and authenticity, aiming for good presence in big formats and efficiency in small ones.

name: Mexica
classification_notes: Designed around Nahuatl's diagonal-heavy orthography (abundant X Y Z, absent rounded B D G) rather than a Latin-first letterform brief.
summary: A contemporary serif tuned to the diagonal-heavy orthography of Nahuatl, the Aztec lingua franca of ancient Mexico.
description: Mexica is a typographic tribute to Nahuatl, whose classic orthography abounds in diagonal X Y Z shapes and lacks rounded letters like B D G. Long compound words common to the language shaped the design, alongside daring, stylish serif detailing across several weights and small caps.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Mexica as designed to perform as a contemporary, daring, stylish serif family suited to Nahuatl's distinctive visual features.

name: Milanesa Serif
classification_notes: A serif that shifts its contrast angle toward the black end of its range, giving each weight a distinct interpolated character rather than a simple linear scale.
summary: A seven-weight serif that shifts its contrast angle toward the black end, intensifying its forms as it gets heavier.
description: Milanesa Serif undergoes something close to a metamorphosis across its weights, varying counterforms and intensifying its forms without losing the family's sense of cohesion. It suits versatile applications from web design to editorial and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Milanesa Serif as keeping the traditional canon in a serif while playing with a modern concept to impose its versatility.

name: Milk Script
classification_notes: Unearthed from a 1923 Speedball lettering manual, an upright script offered with an optional non-connecting variant for extra aesthetic control.
summary: A distinctive upright script unearthed from a 1923 Speedball lettering manual, with a non-connecting variant for extra control.
description: Milk Script offers well-nourished majuscules and sweet-flowing minuscules, drawing on the hand-lettered signage of 1920s and 1930s America. Alfredo Graziani and Alejandro Paul unearthed the source material and digitised it as a distinctive typographic jewel.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Milk Script one of many typographic jewels from 1920s and 1930s American hand-lettered signage that digital type has yet to fully manifest.

name: Milonguita
classification_notes: An irregular, energetic script channelling the short, lively movements of Argentine milonga dancing rather than tango's more nostalgic feel.
summary: An irregular, energetic script channelling the light-hearted, quick movements of Argentine milonga dancing.
description: Milonguita lets readers play with upward and downward letter patterns to create different images and textures, its irregular strokes conveying emotion and a bond between font and writer. The result combines elegance, energy and rhythm.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Milonguita as designed so readers can experience the passion and spontaneity of the milonga dancing style through words.

name: Ministry Script
classification_notes: Built from a how-to lettering book but developed into a complex modern digital design, positioned as a time capsule bridging 1920s American ad art and contemporary type technology.
summary: A time-capsule script marking both 1920s American ad art and contemporary digital type acrobatics.
description: Ministry Script's first letters came from a how-to lettering book before growing into a complex, modern typeface with over 1,000 characters and four variants of each letter accessible through OpenType. It was selected for inclusion in Paul McNeil's book "The Visual History of Type", among 350 typefaces of all time.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Ministry Script as a time capsule marking both the American ad art of the 1920s and new-millennium digital type acrobatics.

summary: A Bluemlein Script Collection revival under the invented name Miss Blaker Pro, built for elegant backslant invitations and stationery.
description: Miss Blaker Pro belongs to the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, a set of alphabets built by collecting individual signatures from professional New York hand letterers of the 1930s and 1940s, an occupation that disappeared with the rise of photo and digital lettering. foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Mister Giacco Pro a simple stroke sans serif font ideal for corporate use, branding and any design where legibility and personality are required.

name: Mobley
classification_notes: Rebuilds ten characters from a 1960s Blue Note jazz album cover, originally Wayne Stettler's Neil Bold for Visual Graphics Corporation, into a complete sans-and-serif system.
summary: A bold, friendly display face rebuilt from ten characters found on a 1960s Blue Note jazz album cover.
description: Mobley Sans and its condensed and serifed counterparts form a new typographic whole molded around Wayne Stettler's original Neil Bold source characters. Odd counters, generous curves and sharp corners give it the independent creative spirit of its era with contemporary detail, suited to music artwork, packaging and book covers.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos describes Mobley as delivering its message in a bold, yet friendly and subtly discerning fashion, perfect for music artwork, packaging and book covers.

name: Mon Nicolette
classification_notes: A digital revival of William Addison Dwiggins's unfinished Charter typeface, an upright, unconnected italic script with pronounced contrast and condensed forms.
summary: A digital completion of William Addison Dwiggins's unfinished Charter, an upright, condensed italic script left incomplete since 1955.
description: Dwiggins worked on Charter from 1937 to 1955 but only ever completed the lowercase and a few other characters, using it to set a 1942 specimen and a 1946 short novel. Cristóbal Henestrosa based Mon Nicolette on Dwiggins's original sketches and Boston Public Library printing trials, completing the family across Petite and Grande optical sizes plus a display Toscane style, suited to headlines and short passages from 12 points up.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos frames Mon Nicolette as a digital revival based on Charter, an experimental typeface designed but never fully accomplished by William Addison Dwiggins.

summary: A revival of Glenmoy, a 1932 Stephenson Blake display face from the golden age of pre-WWII American advertising.
description: Mousse Script expands Glenmoy's limited metal character set to nearly double its original size using current type technology, keeping the striking, functional display quality that once sold countless magazine products before the trend shifted to handwritten calligraphic styles.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos calls Mousse Script's source, Glenmoy, a prime example of pre-WWII American ad art display typography, now brought back and expanded.

summary: A Bluemlein Script Collection revival under the invented name Mr Sandsfort Pro, built for elegant vintage stationery lettering.
description: Mr Sandsfort Pro belongs to the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, a set of alphabets built by collecting individual signatures from professional New York hand letterers of the 1930s and 1940s, an occupation that disappeared with the rise of photo and digital lettering. Sudtipos expanded the originals into modern digital versions for elegant vintage stationery lettering.
foundry_blurb: Sudtipos revives the Charles Bluemlein Script Collection, assembled by collecting different signatures and building complete alphabets from them, then presented under fictitious names in Higgins Ink catalogs.
